name: Madagascar Pochard
rangeDescription: Lac alaotra and lac matsaborimena (north-central and northwestern madagascar, respectively); thought extinct until rediscovered at lac matsaborimena in 2006
description: Extremely rare diving duck that was long thought extinct before being rediscovered in 2006 in a remote site in northern Madagascar. A large duck that is mostly rich brown, with white under the tail.

name: Malabar Gray Hornbill
rangeDescription: Moist deciduous forest of southwestern india
description: A small gray hornbill with a casque-less pale bill, a black undertail with white tips, and a pale eyebrow. Sexes are alike, except that the females have black on the base of the bill.

name: Trocaz Pigeon
rangeDescription: Laurel forest of madeira
description: Endemic to the island of Madeira, where it is largely restricted to native laurel and tree heath forests. Body is largely gray with a purple-pink breast, and a noticeable silvery patch with black streaks on the side of the neck.

name: Orange-crowned Euphonia
rangeDescription: Colombia on both slopes of western andes (southward from southern chocó and risaralda), western ecuador, and extreme northwestern peru (tumbes)
description: Small finchlike bird, compact and short tailed with a stout bill. Male has notably orange-tinged underparts and dark upperparts with a purplish sheen.

name: Dotted Tanager
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela to the guianas and northern amazonian brazil
description: Small, beautiful tanager with bright uniform green plumage. Males have bluish wings and tail and scattered dots on breast.

name: Pied-winged Swallow
rangeDescription: Savanna of western africa (senegambia to far western cameroon)
description: A small martin-like swallow with pale underparts, steel-blue upperparts, and distinctive white patches in the wings. Female has a shorter tail than the male.

name: Santa Marta Woodstar
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Tiny bumblebee-like hummingbird found only in and around Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains, where it is the only woodstar. Usually encountered in cloud forest at moderate elevations, but occasionally wanders down to near sea level.

name: Oahu Elepaio
rangeDescription: Oahu (hawaiian islands)
description: A small flycatcher of forested habitats on Oahu. Adults are brown above, whitish below, and have white wingbars, rump, and tail tips.

name: Sumatran Ground-Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Lowlands and foothills of southwestern sumatra (basiran mountains)
description: Incredibly elusive and rare, this is a highly sought-after ground-dweller. Found only in primary hill forest (300-1400 meters) in western Sumatra.

name: Cameroon Speirops
rangeDescription: Montane forest of mount cameroon
description: A dull dark brown white-eye with a distinctive white forecrown, white eye-ring and throat, and pale bill and legs; eyes are also often pale. A local but common resident restricted to Mount Cameroon, found in small groups between 1800 and 2800 meters of elevation.

name: Gray-fronted Quail-Dove
rangeDescription: Cuba (rare)
description: A multicolored chunky dove of dense, wet forests with thick leaf-litter. It is most often found on the ground, sometimes in association with Blue-headed or Ruddy Quail-Doves.

name: Bar-winged Weaver
rangeDescription: Angola to northern zambia and far southeastern democratic republic of the congo
description: A localized woodland weaver that has dark brown upperparts, yellow back and rump, obvious white wing bars, and pale underparts suffused with lemon on the belly and flanks. Juvenile is like adult but with a pale crown and bill.

name: Bee Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: This tiny nectar sipper is the world’s smallest bird. It feeds on woodland flowers, especially those that are more horizontally positioned.

name: Ochre-collared Monarch
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northern new guinea, including yapen (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A slender, medium-sized bird of lowland and foothill forest. Fairly long tail and black face with gray bill and blue eye wattle.

name: Rufous-naped Tit
rangeDescription: Southern uzbekistan, tajikistan, and kyrgyzstan, northwestern china (western xinjiang), northwestern and eastern afghanistan, western and northern pakistan, and eastward in himalayas to west-central nepal (kali gandaki gorge)
description: Small, dark, crested tit of montane and hilly coniferous forests. Lack of white on the wings (except for large cheek patch) and erect crest separate it from Coal Tit.

name: Semicollared Hawk
rangeDescription: Mountains of colombia to southwestern venezuela, ecuador, and southern peru
description: Tiny, rare hawk of mid-elevation cloud forest. Black upperparts and crown are separated by white band on back of neck, which can be indistinct and hard to see in the field.

name: Black-headed Gonolek
rangeDescription: Acacia of nigeria to sudan, ethiopia, kenya, and northwestern tanzania
description: Boldly patterned black-and-red bushshrike with pale eyes. The immature has pale underparts with fine dark bars.

name: Orange Chat
rangeDescription: Interior of australia, to southern and western coasts
description: Brightly colored, terrestrial songbird found in open and arid regions across much of inland Australia. Male has rich bright orange head and underparts, with a dramatic throat that extends to the dark eye.
imageCreditName: Laurie Ross | Tracks Birding & Photography Tours

name: Black-headed Jay
rangeDescription: Himalayas (afghanistan to northern india and central nepal)
description: Largely gray with a black head, a scruffy crest, white streaks on the throat, and a pale bill. The wings and tail are blue through the middle with black barring, leading to thick black and white bands.

name: Salvin's Curassow
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of southern colombia to eastern ecuador and northeastern peru
description: Large black curassow with a bright red bill, white lower belly, and white tail tip. Unlikely to be confused.
